evals.name: codebase-question
evals.prompt: Our billing team keeps saying jobqueue never loses an invoice job. I'm not convinced. The repo is at {REPO}. Can you research what actually happens to a job if a worker process dies halfway through running it, and write it up as a research doc in the repo? Don't change any code.
evals.expected_output: A new docs/research/0002-*.md at status draft that passes the checker. Findings: dequeue uses BLPOP, which removes the job before the handler runs, so a worker crash loses it (High/Medium, cited to jobqueue/queue.py and worker.py); retries only cover handler exceptions, so the README's at-least-once claim does not hold for a crash. Sources are repo files. No code changed, no ADR written.
assertions: A new research document exists at docs/research/0002-<slug>.md, numbered after the existing 0001, and 0001 is untouched
`research.py check` exits 0 on the new document
A finding states that a job is lost when the worker dies after dequeuing it, because dequeue (BLPOP) removes the job from Redis before the handler runs
That finding is rated High or Medium and cites jobqueue/queue.py or jobqueue/worker.py as a codebase source
The document says the README's at-least-once delivery claim does not hold for a worker crash, noting that retries only cover exceptions raised by the handler
Every source is a repo file that exists, an experiment that was actually run, or an external page the run actually opened; none is an invented URL
The new document's frontmatter status is draft
No file outside docs/research was created or modified: no code change and no ADR
The Conclusions do not choose a fix; any remedy is offered as what the evidence supports, or the choice is left to an ADR

evals.name: decision-in-disguise
evals.prompt: We're deciding whether to move jobqueue (repo at {REPO}) from Redis to SQS. Research it and tell us which one we should go with, and we'll record whatever you pick.
evals.expected_output: A research document comparing how the current Redis implementation and SQS behave against the job-loss concern, with the research question phrased as something that can be answered by looking. Conclusions give a recommendation at most and say the choice belongs in an ADR. No ADR is written. Claims about SQS are cited to something actually opened or rated Low.
assertions: A new research document exists in docs/research and `research.py check` exits 0 on it
No new ADR was created: docs/adr still holds only 0001
The Research Question asks what is true (for example how the two compare on job loss for this workload), not which one to choose
The Method states plainly whether external sources (documentation or the web) were consulted
Every finding about SQS either cites an external source with an accessed date or is rated Low; none is rated High on the strength of recall alone
A finding records the current Redis behaviour from the repo: a job is lost if the worker dies after dequeuing it
The Conclusions, at most, make a recommendation, and say that making the choice belongs in an ADR
The final report names create-adr (or an ADR) as the next step for the choice

evals.name: already-answered
evals.prompt: Repo at {REPO}. Before the monthly Redis patching next week, can you look into whether jobs sitting in the queue survive a Redis restart? Write it up.
evals.expected_output: No new document. The run finds docs/research/0001 already answers the question, redis.conf has not changed since, so it is still fresh; it reports that document and its key finding and leaves it untouched.
assertions: No new file was created in docs/research: it still holds only 0001
The response identifies docs/research/0001-queued-jobs-survive-redis-restart.md (RES-0001) as already answering the question
The response relays the answer: pending jobs survive a clean restart, and a hard crash can lose up to about a second of enqueues
The response says the existing research is still current, because redis.conf has not changed since it was written (its Revisit When condition has not been met)
RES-0001 was not modified

evals.name: stale-supersede
evals.prompt: Repo at {REPO}. I switched redis.conf to `appendonly no` last week to cut disk IO. The research doc on whether queued jobs survive a Redis restart was written before that. Redo the research so our docs are right.
evals.setup: In the copied repo, change redis.conf so that `appendonly yes` reads `appendonly no`. Everything else is unchanged.
evals.expected_output: A new docs/research/0002-*.md with supersedes: [RES-0001] that finds pending jobs no longer survive a restart (persistence off: appendonly no, save empty). RES-0001 gets status superseded and superseded-by: [RES-0002], with its findings and conclusions left as written. Both documents pass the checker.
assertions: A new research document exists at docs/research/0002-<slug>.md and `research.py check` exits 0 on it
The new document lists RES-0001 in its `supersedes` frontmatter
RES-0001 now has status superseded and RES-0002 in its `superseded-by`, and `research.py check` exits 0 on it
RES-0001's Findings, Conclusions and Sources are byte-for-byte unchanged; only its status and superseded-by lines differ
A finding in the new document says pending jobs are not kept across a Redis restart now that appendonly is no (and save is empty), rated High, citing redis.conf
The new document's Revisit When names a concrete condition (for example any change to persistence settings), not just None

evals.name: topic-not-question
evals.prompt: Repo at {REPO}. Can you do some research on caching for us? We'll want it written up in docs.
evals.expected_output: No document is scaffolded. The run recognises 'caching' is a topic, not a question, and asks at most three focused questions in one round, each with concrete options and a recommended first option, grounded in what this repo is (invoice jobs on Redis).
assertions: No research document was created: docs/research still holds only 0001
The response asks the user to narrow the request, rather than producing a survey of caching approaches
The response asks at most three questions
Each question offers concrete options, with a recommended option first, rather than being open-ended
At least one question or option refers to something specific to this repo (for example the invoice jobs, Redis, or the queue) rather than caching in general
